Head_and_Face: Head has a single pair of eyes positioned dorsally on a small turret (ocularium).
Mouthparts are small chelicerae used for chewing.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is small, rounded, and compact with a fused cephalothorax and abdomen (no narrow waist).
Body coloration is dark brown to black with a smooth, glossy surface.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Eight extremely elongated, thread-like legs; legs are disproportionately long relative to body size.
Second pair of legs is the longest and used as sensory organs.
No silk-producing glands or fangs.

Head_and_Face: Cephalothorax bears a pair of large, pincer-like pedipalps (claws) at the anterior end.
Pedipalps are robust and heavily sclerotized with spiny inner margins.
Body_and_Plumage: Body consists of a cephalothorax (prosoma) and segmented abdomen (opisthosoma).
Body coloration is yellow-brown to black with a smooth, glossy exoskeleton.
Body surface is smooth with fine granular texture.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Four pairs of walking legs extend from the cephalothorax; legs are slender with terminal claws.
Elongated, segmented tail (metasoma) comprising five segments ending in a bulbous telson (stinger).
Tail curves upward and forward over the back in a characteristic defensive posture.

Head_and_Face: Eyes are small and arranged in two rows.
Body_and_Plumage: Cephalothorax is covered in dense silver-white hairs creating a silvery appearance.
Abdomen is large and oval with a striking pattern: black background with four to five pairs of yellow spots arranged symmetrically.
Yellow spots are bright and contrasting.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Legs are long and banded with alternating black and yellow rings.
Legs are covered in fine spines.
Constructs a large, circular orb web with a distinctive zigzag stabilimentum running vertically through the center.

Head_and_Face: Eyes are small and arranged in two rows.
Body_and_Plumage: Cephalothorax is yellowish-brown with a distinct white longitudinal stripe running down the midline.
Abdomen is large and oval with a mottled pattern of orange, tan, and brown.
Dorsal surface has a leaf-like marking in darker brown.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Legs are long and banded with alternating dark and light rings.
Legs are covered in fine spines and hairs.
Constructs a large, circular orb web typically in sheltered locations such as barns, eaves, or window frames.

Head_and_Face: Eyes are small and arranged in two rows.
Body_and_Plumage: Cephalothorax is brownish-grey with fine hairs.
Abdomen is large and oval with a dark brown background and a prominent white or cream-colored cross-shaped marking (crucifix pattern) on the dorsal surface.
The cross is formed by intersecting bands creating a distinctive cruciform shape.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Legs are long and banded with alternating dark and light rings.
Legs are covered in fine spines.
Constructs a large, circular orb web often including a zigzag stabilimentum running vertically through the center.

Body_and_Plumage: Body is entirely jet black with a smooth, highly glossy, almost lacquered appearance.
Bright red hourglass-shaped marking on the ventral (underside) surface of the abdomen.
Hourglass consists of two triangular red patches connected at the apex, creating a symmetrical hourglass shape.
Some individuals have additional red spots on the dorsal surface of the abdomen.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Legs are long, slender, and uniformly black without banding.
Legs are smooth without spines.
Constructs an irregular, tangled web close to the ground in dark, sheltered locations.

Head_and_Face: Eight eyes arranged in a compact group at the front of the cephalothorax.
Chelicerae (fangs) are large and prominent, projecting downward.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is massive and heavily-built.
Body coloration varies by species: common colors include black, brown, grey, or iridescent blue-green.
Most distinctive feature is the dense covering of long, bristly hairs (setae) over the entire body and legs, creating a furry appearance.
Cephalothorax and abdomen are covered in dense, velvety hairs.
Some species have urticating (irritating) hairs on the abdomen.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Legs are thick and robust.
Many species are terrestrial burrowers.

Head_and_Face: Most distinctive feature is the eye arrangement: eight eyes arranged in three rows (four small eyes in the front row, two large eyes in the middle row, and two medium eyes in the back row).
The two large median eyes are prominent and forward-facing.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is robust and hairy.
Body coloration is grey, brown, or black with longitudinal stripes or mottled patterning.
Cephalothorax is broad and flat with a distinct longitudinal stripe running down the midline.
Abdomen is oval and covered in dense hairs with variable patterning.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Legs are long and robust, covered in spines and hairs, adapted for rapid running.
Does not construct a web; hunts by actively pursuing prey on the ground.

Head_and_Face: Barbed proboscis (hypostome) projecting from the anterior end, covered in backward-pointing barbs.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is flattened and oval when unfed, becoming engorged and spherical after feeding.
Body coloration is reddish-brown to dark brown with a smooth, leathery exoskeleton.
Cephalothorax and abdomen are fused into a single body unit (idiosoma) without visible segmentation.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Legs are short and stout with eight legs in adults (six in larvae).
Legs terminate in claws and adhesive pads for clinging to hosts.
Exhibits a characteristic questing posture, perched on vegetation with front legs extended.

Head_and_Face: Head is flattened with a pair of long, segmented antennae extending forward.
Body_and_Plumage: Body is flattened and segmented.
Body coloration is yellow-brown to reddish-brown with a smooth, glossy exoskeleton.
Body consists of 15-173 segments, each bearing a single pair of legs.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Modified first pair of legs (forcipules) transformed into venomous claws (poison claws) located beneath the head.
Forcipules are large, curved, and used to capture and immobilize prey.
Legs are long and slender, extending laterally from the body.
Last pair of legs is often elongated and held backward, resembling antennae.
